questions.q: In what order are the pieces of a sharded cluster typically brought up?
options: Config server replica set, then shard replica sets, then mongos, then shards are registered
mongos first, then shards, then config servers last
All pieces must start simultaneously or the cluster fails
Shards first, config servers are optional
questions.explain: The metadata and routing layers exist before data gets distributed, so config servers come up first, followed by shard replica sets and mongos.

questions.q: What startup flag marks a mongod instance as a config server replica set member?
options: --shardsvr
--mongos
--configsvr
--replSet only
questions.explain: --configsvr designates a mongod as part of the config server replica set, distinct from --shardsvr used for shard members.

options: Applies the shard key to a collection
Creates the config server replica set
Registers a shard's replica set with a running sharded cluster
Starts the mongos process
questions.explain: Once mongos is running and pointed at the config servers, each shard's replica set is registered with the cluster using sh.addShard().

questions.q: What does sh.shardCollection() do, and what does it require as an argument?
options: Enables sharding on a specific collection, using a chosen shard key
Enables sharding cluster-wide with no key needed
Adds a new node to a replica set
Deletes an existing sharded collection
questions.explain: sh.shardCollection() takes the collection name and the shard key definition, e.g. sh.shardCollection('appdb.orders', { customerId: 'hashed' }).

questions.q: Once a collection is sharded, what does a DBA's ongoing job look like, per this lesson?
options: Re-running sh.shardCollection() daily
Monitoring chunk balance and migration health, since mongos and config servers split/migrate chunks automatically
Nothing — sharded clusters require no ongoing attention ever
Manually moving every document to the correct shard by hand
questions.explain: mongos and the config servers automatically split and migrate chunks as data grows and shifts, shifting the DBA's role toward monitoring.
